correctness.rationale: The digit valuation rule yields parity-invariant offsets between multiples of 2^k and exact endpoint values; all shorter intervals lift to at least three matching positions in P_n. The length-nine synchronization lemma is proved by complete symbolic 36-template enumeration, not an inductive guess. At dyadic scales k>=3, exact even-position decimation and p(2i)=p(i) prove no aligned factor can occur unaligned. The eight endpoint-triple classes have exactly two singletons. The k=2 base is checked by exhaustive direct counting of all 60 length-five factors of P_6. The standalone checker regenerated the 36 distinct templates and all n=6..12 length-q and q+1 factor multiplicities. Boundary indexing, k=2, and the infinite/finite distinction were reconstructed and checked; finite tests are not treated as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Exact first-unique-factor threshold and complete locations for regular paperfolding dyadic prefixes are not implied by the closely related complete Fibonacci/Thue-Morse minimal unique substring theorem (different infinite word), the Fibonacci/period-doubling attractor characterizations (different invariant), the paperfolding infinite factor-complexity formula (no multiplicities in finite prefixes), or published regular-paperfolding attractor computations. published-finding corpus queries for paperfolding, minimum unique factors, aliases, positions, and dyadic synchronization retrieved no equivalent stronger claim. This is conditional best-knowledge originality, not a uniqueness guarantee; SCOPE079 full record and some unindexed sources were not inspected completely.

value.rationale: In recent work minimal unique substrings are studied as exact occurrence statistics of structured words. The paperfolding sequence is a classical morphic/automatic sequence with exact infinite factor complexity but finite-prefix multiplicities are a different invariant. The theorem completely classifies the precise minimum length, both unique factors and their positions for an infinite dyadic family, using an illuminating finite synchronization certificate followed by a two-adic induction. The specific powers-of-two family is natural and its answer is not a routine recomputation of the known infinite factor table or optimal attractor counts.
